editorial:
After his mother dies, a boy called Zucchini is taken to a foster home by a kind police officer named Raymond. There he meets other kids who also carry big feelings, and the story follows his slow journey toward trust, friendship, and a new family. The movie is warm, sad, funny, and gentle all at once. Its stop-motion world feels handmade and alive, and the children act like real kids instead of perfect heroes. You feel their loneliness, but you also feel their hope as they learn to care for each other.

The animation is charming, the voice acting feels natural, and the pacing moves quickly without rushing the emotions. Pros include honest feelings, sweet humor, and beautiful craft. Cons include a short runtime and themes that may be too heavy for very young viewers. It is a great pick for adults, teens, and families with older kids. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Zucchini and his friends grow closer, and Raymond stays a steady support. A new girl, Camille, arrives and connects with Zucchini. The kids face the possibility of being separated, but they choose to stay together as a family. In the end, Zucchini finds a real home with Raymond and Camille, showing that love can grow from loss and friendship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt animation and stories about found family.
